- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day windows.
- Underestimate mid-to-late horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment remains flat or slightly negative.
- Avoid sharp downward corrections after upward spikes; if forecast exceeds true value by >3%, apply a “mean reversion” dampening factor to subsequent days.
- If sentiment history is all zero (neutral), assume no sentiment-driven bias; apply a “baseline correction” to align forecast with recent 7-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show consistent overestimation, reduce the first 5–7 forecast values by 1–2% to match observed mean reversion behavior.
- If true outcome shows a sharp upward move after a forecast peak, reduce forecast for next 3–5 days by 1–2% to avoid “overshoot” bias.
- When sentiment is zero, do not apply sentiment-based adjustments; rely on historical mean and volatility to correct forecast drift.
